heading: WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
translated_text:
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

Revision of Discussion Results May 22, 2019.

REGENT OF TASIKMALAYA

WEST JAVA PROVINCE

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF TASIKMALAYA REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya.
2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya.
3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
12. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household.
16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
17. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations.
20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business determined by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service.
21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area.
22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect.
23. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect.
24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
25. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly.
29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems;
31. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
32. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT), Integrated Service Centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, Science and Technology Information Centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.
33. Women and Child Protection Task Force is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Sub-district level.
34. Women and Child Protection Task Unit is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Village level.
35. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
36. Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is a coordinative institution at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.
37. Regional Action Plan for Child-Friendly Regency Development is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 2

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the implementation of women's empowerment.
2. Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, budgets, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.

heading: Article 3

Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

The implementation of women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in Article 3 letter d includes:
a. improvement of knowledge and awareness in the legal field through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and consultation services as well as free legal aid.

heading: CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights domestically or abroad receive protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide protection to women in order to realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.
2. Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Child Protection in the Field of Religion and Belief

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. Every child receives protection to worship according to their respective religion and belief.
2. Before the child can determine their choice, the religion embraced by the child follows the religion of their parents.
3. In the case of child adoption, prospective adoptive parents must have the same religion as the religion embraced by the prospective adopted child.
4. If the origin of the child as referred to in paragraph (3) is not known, then the child's religion is adjusted to the religion of the majority of the local population.

CHAPTER V
Article 26
heading_path: FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

heading: CHAPTER VI
Article 28
CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Part One

General

heading: Article 29
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Regional Government

heading: Article 30
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Village Government

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. prepare and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to the village's financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government prepares programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Community

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Parents, Guardians and/or Family

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to report if violence occurs and to protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or for some reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members which shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

General

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

The Regional Government carries out activities for the implementation of protection of women and protection of children, which include:
a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. social rehabilitation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Prevention

heading: Article 35
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Services

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

Services as referred to in Article 34 letter b, take into account:
a. service principles; and
b. forms of services to victims.

heading: Article 37
Article 38
Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

Complaint, consultation and counseling services as referred to in Article 38 letter a number 1, include:
a. identification or initial recording of victims; and
b. informed consent.

heading: Article 40
Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

Health services as referred to in Article 38 letter a number 3 include:
a. first aid to victims by competent officers;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services as needed.

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

1. Legal aid services as referred to in Article 38 letter a number 4 are to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
2. Legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully explain the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

heading: Article 43
Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Social Rehabilitation

heading: Article 44
translated_text:
Article 44

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 34 letter c is a service provided by assistants to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who need continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus that have principal tasks and functions in the implementation of affairs:
a. social;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
5. In addition to being implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

Article 46

Part Six

Regional Indonesian Child Protection Commission

heading: Article 50
translated_text:
Article 50

1. The Regional Indonesian Child Protection Commission as referred to in Article 45 letter e is a partner of the Government in the effort to fulfill children's rights and child protection and is positioned at the Regency level.
2. The Regional Indonesian Child Protection Commission shall be stipulated by Regent's decree.
3. The membership of the Regional Indonesian Child Protection Commission consists of 1 (one) chairperson, 1 (one) vice chairperson, and 7 (seven) members. (4) The membership of the Regional Indonesian Child Protection Commission comes from elements of the Regional Government, religious leaders, community leaders, community organizations, business sector, and community groups that care about child protection.

heading: Article 51
Part Seven
translated_text:
Part Seven

Regional Children's Forum

heading: Article 52
translated_text:
Article 52

1. The Regional Children's Forum as referred to in Article 45 letter f is an organization or social institution used as a forum or institution for the participation of children who are not yet 18 (eighteen) years old where its members are representatives of children's groups or children's activity groups managed by children and fostered by the government as a medium to hear and fulfill the aspirations, voices, opinions, desires and needs of children in the development process.
2. The Regional Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be established in tiers at all levels, namely:
a. Regency Level;
b. Sub-District Level; and
c. Village Level.

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Children's Forum at Regency Level

heading: Article 53
translated_text:
Article 53

1. The Regency Level Children's Forum as referred to in Article 52 paragraph (2) letter a is a forum for children's participation in the Regency area whose members consist of representatives of the Sub-district Level Children's Forum of at least 1 (one) girl and 1 (one) boy.
2. The Regency Level Children's Forum is established by Regent's Decree with a management period of 2 (two) years.
3. In order for the Regency Level Children's Forum to function properly, a secretariat must be formed.
4. The formation of the secretariat as referred to in paragraph (3) may involve at most 40% (forty percent) of unmarried adults.
5. The involvement of adults as referred to in paragraph (4) is intended to guide and foster new members in the Regency Level Children's Forum.
6. The Regency Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment and child protection as the Supervisor of the Regency Level Children's Forum facilitates the formation of the Regency Level Children's Forum starting from the election stage, ratification of management and guidance in capacity building of members of the Regency Level Children's Forum.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Sub-district Level Children's Forum

heading: Article 54
translated_text:
Article 54

1. The Sub-district Level Children's Forum as referred to in Article 52 paragraph (2) letter b is a forum for children's participation in the sub-district area whose members consist of representatives of the Village Level Children's Forum of at least 1 (one) girl and 1 (one) boy.
2. The Sub-district Level Children's Forum is established by Sub-district Head's Decree with a management period of 2 (two) years.
3. The Sub-district Government as the Supervisor of the Sub-district Level Children's Forum facilitates the formation of the Sub-district Level Children's Forum starting from the election stage, ratification of management and guidance in capacity building of members of the Sub-district Level Children's Forum.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Village Level Children's Forum

heading: Article 55
translated_text:
Article 55

1. The Village Level Children's Forum as referred to in Article 52 paragraph (2) letter c is a forum for children's participation in the Village area whose members consist of representatives from Neighborhood Units and Community Units of at least 1 (one) girl and 1 (one) boy.
2. The Village Level Children's Forum is established by Village Head's Decree with a management period of 2 (two) years.
3. The Village Government as the Supervisor of the Village Level Children's Forum facilitates the formation of the Village Level Children's Forum starting from the election stage, ratification of management and guidance in capacity building of members of the Village Level Children's Forum.
4. Community institutions existing in the Village have the obligation to accommodate and foster children's participation in development and in advocating for children's rights.

heading: CHAPTER X
Article 57
Article 58
Article 59
translated_text:
Article 59

1. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in Article 58 paragraph (3) letter b shall be prepared for a period of 5 (five) years or according to needs integrated with the regional medium-term development plan and the work plan of regional apparatus.
2. The Regional Action Plan shall have an annual program focus that refers to the stages of achieving Child-Friendly Regency indicators.
3. The Child-Friendly Regency Regional Action Plan must be based on problems in the field and their comprehensive resolution.
4. The Regional Action Plan shall be disseminated to all Regional Apparatus, child stakeholders, families, and the community.
5. Further provisions regarding the Child-Friendly Regency Regional Action Plan shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND REPORTING

Article 60

Monitoring shall be conducted periodically and in an integrated manner every 6 (six) months by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in coordination with Regional Apparatus or other units that handle women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 61
translated_text:
Article 61

Evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection at least 2 (two) times in 1 (one) year.

heading: Article 62
CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

FUNDING

Article 63

Funding for women's empowerment and child protection shall be sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget;
b. village revenue and expenditure budget; and
c. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that have the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at Sub-district Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 65

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. So that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Tasikmalaya Regency.
